about: The rules of the lot judge (Lucie, 24 November 2026: « qu'il sorte un rapport des choses qui violent les règles : des trucs hardcodés, pas en anglais, ou mal templatisés »). The judge reads a lot's diff (origin/master...head), the repository's AGENTS.md and these rules, and gives findings; it blocks nothing. The lot may also carry subject (the titles of its commits) and recent_master_added: the lines master added recently in the files the lot touches, for the rule reverted_master_change. Each rule has an id, the question the judge answers on the diff's added lines, its severity, and examples of what violates it.

rules.question: Does an added line hard-code a list of commands, programs, providers, model names, file extensions or hosts in code, where a template, a rules file or a declared graph would hold it?
violates: a match arm per provider name
a const array of command names in Rust
a model slug written in a test or in code instead of read from the registry

rules.question: Does an added line write a model name or a provider in code or in a test (gemini-…, claude-…, gpt-…, vertex, anthropic, a model slug), where the registry (models.llm) or a declared template should name it?
violates: a test that sets the model to "gemini-3"
match provider { "vertex" => … }

rules.question: Does an added line DECLARE an identifier that is not English: a fn, a let, a struct or enum, a field, a const, a parameter, a JSON key, a script variable, a test name, a file, a route, a node type? A declaration in an added line counts even when the name looks short or common. A name that is only called or used in an added line, declared elsewhere, never counts. Prose, comments and user-facing texts in French are fine.
violates: let index_pose = …
let est = …
fn pas_en_cours(…)
let chemin = …
let outils = …
fn avec_theme(…)

rules.question: Does an added line write, in code, a text meant for a language model (a prompt, a system message, a relaunch, a refusal sent back to the model) instead of reading it from a template file?
violates: format!("You are a teammate…")
a refusal text built in Rust and returned as a tool result

rules.question: Does an added Rust function compose several decisions (conditions chained by if/else, a priority list of guards, a policy) where a declared graph (conditions, FirstMatch, Decide, Route) would do, instead of a primitive node that does one thing?
violates: a step_done that checks text, tools, plan and mailbox in one function
a match over verdicts that decides what to do in code

rules.question: Does the lot add or change behaviour without a witness that could fail on the old code: a test that only checks that something compiles, a test that passes on master too, a fix without a failing test committed before it?
violates: a test whose assertions hold before the change
a fix commit with no red commit before it

rules.question: Does the diff break a rule of AGENTS.md (a mention of an AI assistant in a commit message or a file, a heavy run without the machine lock, a known defect left without a ticket)?
violates: Co-Authored-By: an assistant
cargo test -j$(nproc) in a script

rules.question: Does the lot REMOVE lines it should not: lines in files the lot's announced subject (subject: the titles of its commits) does not explain, lines that a recent commit of master had just added (recent_master_added, when given), or a rule, a guard or a test without replacing it? A removal the subject announces (a commit title that says it removes, moves or replaces that rule or that code) is not a finding. Give one finding per file, its excerpt being the first removed line, and say in why how many lines are removed there. This is the one rule that reads the removed lines.
violates: a repose of a lot about a page that removes 52 lines of teammate.rs
a repose that removes the end-of-turn rule master added an hour before
a guard deleted in a lot about something else
